To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we measured the first Be-9(e,e') spectra at an electron energy E0= 73 MeV with high-energy resolution, that we extracted the resonance parameters of the 1/2(+), 1.75 MeV resonance, which are in excellent agreement with the latest (n, gamma) experiment but with much better uncertainties, and that the reduced B(E-1) transition strength is smaller by a significant factor of 2 than the extrapolation of the data to the photon energy
we have determined resonance parameters of the astrophysically important first excited state in Be-9, which is a key ingredient in stellar nucleosynthesis calculations.

the astrophysically important resonance parameters of the 1/2(+), 1.748 MeV state in 9 Be have been extracted with improved accuracy and the deduced B(E1) strength is a factor of two smaller than previously reported.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of nuclear structure and astrophysics.
the study of the astrophysically interesting Be-9 nucleus, which is a key ingredient of the triple-alpha process, a reaction that leads to the production of C-13 in massive stars.
the investigation of nuclear structure properties of light nuclei, in particular of neutron-rich nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new resonance parameters are consistent with those from the (g, n) reaction, and the new B(E1) is smaller by a large factor.
the new data are in good agreement within the uncertainties with the results of the (gamma, n) experiment, but the (e, n) data are still in disagreement.

the resonance parameters of the Be-7(p, gamma) reaction, which is of astrophysical interest for the production of C-8 and C-12 in the Big Bang and in novae, are not yet fully established and require further experimental and theoretical studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our new results on the resonance parameters of the Be-8(n, gamma) resonance are consistent with the latest Be(gamma, n), but our results on the B(E1) strength of the Be-10(gamma) decay are smaller by about a factor of two.

our new data on Be-9(e(e),e') and the new data on Be(gamma, n), both with improved uncertainties, do not allow to reconcile the discrepancy between the two data sets for the reduced transition strength of the 1/2(+)(1.75 MeV) state in Be-9.

the new Be-9(e,e') data are consistent with the new Be-8(p, gamma)C-9 experiment and the new Be-7(p, gamma)Li-8 experiment, and that the new data are inconsistent with the Be-7(n,alpha)Li-4 experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new data on the Be-9(1/2(+)) resonance are consistent with the latest Be(gamma,n) measurements but with considerably smaller uncertainties.
the Be-9 resonance energy is higher than previously thought, and the width is narrower, which implies a higher temperature for CNO burning to occur.
the resonance energy is well determined, but the resonance width and the reduced B(E-1) transition strength to the ground state of Be-8 remain uncertain.
